title: WeldConstraint
summary: Rigidly joins two parts so they move as one assembly: set Part0 and Part1 and they stay locked together. The modern way to build multi-part structures that survive physics.

properties.name: Part0 / Part1
properties.description: The two parts to join. Both must be set for the weld to act.

properties.name: Enabled
properties.description: Toggle the joint without destroying it.

details.heading: What it locks
details.body: The relative position and orientation of the two parts at the moment the weld is active. Move one, the other follows — they become one physics assembly.

details.heading: Anchoring note
details.body: If either part is anchored, the weld holds the other in place relative to it. Fully anchored pairs don't need welds at all.

explanation.whatItIs: Super-glue between two parts. Once welded, they can't drift apart — the physics engine treats their relative pose as fixed.
explanation.whyItExists: Stacked parts without welds fall apart the moment physics touches them. Welds make multi-part builds solid.
whenToUse: Anything that should move as one rigid body
whenNotToUse: Joints that should BEND or ROTATE — use Motor6D or HingeConstraint
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Part0 ──WeldConstraint── Part1
        (relative pose frozen)

Move Part0 → Part1 follows exactly.
Break the weld (Enabled=false) → they separate.
```
tips: Position parts correctly BEFORE enabling the weld — it locks the current offset
Weld chains: weld everything to a PrimaryPart-like root for predictable Model:PivotTo behavior
Studio's Weld tool automates multi-part welding
commonMistakes: Forgetting to weld and watching the build collapse at runtime
Welding parts that overlap physically → jitter; keep surfaces flush
Assuming welds replicate from the client — build/weld server-side or verify

examples.title: Welding a prop together
examples.code:
local function weldModel(model)
    local primary = model.PrimaryPart
    assert(primary, "Model needs a PrimaryPart")
    for _, descendant in model:GetDescendants() do
        if descendant:IsA("BasePart") and descendant ~= primary then
            local weld = Instance.new("WeldConstraint")
            weld.Part0 = primary
            weld.Part1 = descendant
            weld.Parent = primary
        end
    end
end

weldModel(workspace.Car)
-- Now PivotTo/physics moves the whole car as one.
